en.title: Distinct Lowercase Letters Before the First Uppercase Letter
en.description:
Consider only the text strictly before the first uppercase English letter, and count the distinct lowercase English letters in it; if there is no uppercase letter, consider the whole text. Under this definition, the original site's example aaAbcCABBc should give 1; this site has corrected it.

The input protocol, the ranges added by this site, the examples, and the tests were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input: one line of printable ASCII text of length 0..100000, which may contain spaces; only A..Z and a..z count as letters.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: only aa comes before the first uppercase A, and its only distinct lowercase letter is a; the answer is 1.

Example 2: there is no uppercase letter, and the distinct lowercase letters in the whole text are a, b, c; the answer is 3.

Example 3: the first character is already uppercase, so the prefix is empty; the answer is 0.
hints: Scan until the first uppercase letter and stop there, adding every lowercase letter before it to a set.
